definition: Artificially generated data, often produced by another model or simulation, used to supplement or substitute for real-world training data.
details: Synthetic data is increasingly used to train and fine-tune LLMs, particularly for tasks where high-quality real data is scarce, expensive to collect, or raises privacy concerns.
story: Imagine a chef tasting every ingredient before it goes into the pot, deciding what belongs and what would ruin the broth. Better ingredients make a better meal, and the same is true here. Every machine is shaped by what it was shown, so someone has to choose that material with care. It is the raw material; the model is only ever as good as what it was fed. And that is Synthetic Data — the unglamorous work everything else stands on.
